recent.area: LOWER NIAGARA RIVER
recent.narrative: Strong thunderstorms tracked into the western portion of Lake Ontario, ahead of an approaching cold front. The thunderstorms weakened as they reached the U.S. waters of Lake Ontario, Lake Erie, and the Niagara River. The storms remained just strong enough to require warnings and to produce gusty winds up to 38 knots.

recent.area: LOWER NIAGARA RIVER
recent.narrative: On March 16, a strong area of low pressure tracked across the Central Great Lakes into southeast Ontario and southwest Quebec. Convection developed across Ontario, Lake Erie and Pennsylvania during the late morning hours along a pre-frontal trough associated with the system. As the pre-frontal trough and early convection tracked east toward western New York, conditions became more favorable for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop. Strong to severe thunderstorms caused gusty marine winds on Lake Erie and Lake Ontario.

recent.area: LOWER NIAGARA RIVER
recent.narrative: Thunderstorms that formed over the central Great Lakes during the morning survived and tracked east across western New York by early evening. The most instability was built up just southwest of the region across Ohio and western Pennsylvania which resulted in the most concentrated wind damage occurring over Chautauqua County, while wind damage was more sporadic farther north across western New York. A storm survey was conducted in the following days near Lake Erie State Park in western Chautauqua County, but the damage observed was concluded to be caused by straight line winds.

recent.area: LOWER NIAGARA RIVER
recent.narrative: Impressive storms developed on the converging lake breeze over the Niagara Peninsula in Ontario. These cells slowly tracked eastward toward the Niagara River. Each cell rapidly fell apart as it moved into the United States, however one cell managed to drop nickel sized hail near the Niagara River.

recent.area: HAMLIN BEACH TO SODUS BAY NY BEYOND 5NM OFFSHORE TO US/CANADIAN BORDER
recent.narrative: A strong mid-level trough and weak surface cold front crossed the eastern Great Lakes Monday morning. A line of thunderstorms over southern Ontario moved across Lake Erie and eventually reached the western end of Lake Ontario around daybreak. It then moved down the length of Lake Ontario and into the eastern Lake Ontario region. Surface based instability was mainly confined close to the lake shores, which was an influence of the warm lake waters warming the boundary layer. This resulted in a few strong wind gusts along the shores of Lake Erie and Lake Ontario as the line passed.
